ROUND 1 verified the delivery metadata against reality and found it true: the merge is a genuine single-parent squash with one parent, is an ancestor of origin/main, and carries the W7 delivery title; PR 9755 is MERGED with headRefOid 435d59031c77c0fa421da60b8cc42b7e7a75bbf3 and mergeCommit 0cf48cb0018c08329179f83fd9c626e65dfc8589 and mergedAt 2026-09-27T07:24:43Z, matching the trio exactly; all 13 policy-required checks are success on that head, with the three skipped runs (gsd-governance, release-readiness, test-cross-version) explicitly distinguished from success and confirmed to be outside the required 13; every other field checked out against the policy file, GitHub and git. It re-ran the lint battery and got 23 passed / 2 warnings, 1511 test files with 0 literals, and provenance 952/950/951; it re-ran the focused tests and confirmed 55 and 109; it re-derived the 29 changed .rkt files; and it read both red-first captures and quoted their failing assertions. Then it read the gate and found that the proposal as enumerated could not publish: the validation record's remaining-items owner was still the PENDING sentinel, and the gate hard-rejects a placeholder owner. It proved this rather than asserting it, building the finalized trio in a temp root and running the gate over the proposal verbatim (FAIL, one rejection) and over the proposal plus that single field (PASS). That is the whole of round 1's finding. ROUND 2 checked that the fix was real and complete rather than cosmetic: every string value in the evidence and validation records scanned against the sentinel vocabulary with zero sentinel values surviving, the single mention of PENDING correctly identified as historical prose inside notes describing the round-1 finding, and all four remaining items confirmed to carry gate-vocabulary classifications, non-sentinel owners and substantive rationales. It then re-verified every other field against GitHub and git, confirmed the three records agree with each other field by field, re-ran the lint battery and the focused tests and got the same numbers, compared the recorded RUN-SUMMARY against the captured fast-suite log character for character, confirmed the quoted red-first failure text appears literally in the retained captures, and re-derived the 29-file count. It checked the proposed reviewer identity against the sentinel patterns in both the delivery tool and the gate, and judged it an accurate description of what it was doing rather than a fabricated human. It confirmed the staging copies were byte-identical to the worktree copies, that the publication diff is empty and the empty-diff digest therefore correct, and that git status shows exactly the three evidence paths and nothing else. Finally it finalized a copy in /tmp and ran the gate exactly as the publisher will, obtaining the literal string GSD wave evidence PASS with exit 0 and zero rejections. Two things it declined to do, recorded here rather than papered over: it did not re-run the 27-minute fast suite, verifying the captured log instead, and it did not individually re-compile all 29 changed files, spot-checking a sample and relying on the recorded measurement for the rest. Both gaps are disclosed in the validation record itself, which is the right place for them. It found no demonstrable defect. What this verdict does and does not authorize. It authorizes publishing this binding: recording that W7 was delivered and bound to the campaign under the plan id, on this merge commit, with the checks that were actually run. It does not authorize the v1.00.31 tag, and it is not a re-review of the wave content, which the implementation review record covers over its own fifteen rounds. Release readiness and the full CI-strict tag-publish preflight remain outstanding and are run on clean main after this binding merges; this review does not satisfy either and does not claim to.")
